intro: へ (always read え) points the way: it marks the direction something moves in, an arrow drawn towards a place. Where に pins the point of arrival, へ draws the path towards it; after a verb of motion the two are interchangeable for a destination. Unlike に, へ can be followed by の, which makes it the particle that lets a destination or recipient describe a noun: 母への手紙, a letter to my mother.

skills.rule: With a verb of movement, the place you head towards takes へ (read え); に would also be correct.
skills.explain:
へ marks the direction or destination of movement. It goes with verbs that move something somewhere: 行く, 来る, 帰る, 向かう, 出かける, 引っ越す, 送る. In all of these, に is equally correct for the destination; へ puts a little more weight on the direction and the journey, に on the arrival.

へ is narrower than に. It only works where something actually travels. It cannot mark a time (七時に), the place where something is (部屋に猫がいる), the person you meet or hand something to (友達に会う, 弟に本をあげる), a result (医者になる) or a purpose before a motion verb (買いに行く). If nothing moves along a path, へ is wrong. Something sent to a person does travel, so 先生へメールを送る is fine.

Two more facts: the particle is written へ but pronounced え, and it can combine with は and も to contrast destinations: 東京へは行きません (I am not going to Tokyo, whatever else I do).
patterns: [place] へ [行く / 来る / 帰る]
[direction: 北 / 右 / 前] へ [向かう / 進む]

examples.jp: 学校[がっこう]{へ}行[い]きます。
明日[あした]、東京[とうきょう]{へ}行[い]きます。
examples.en: I am going to Tokyo tomorrow.

examples.jp: 何時[なんじ]にうち{へ}帰[かえ]りますか。
examples.en: What time are you going home?

examples.jp: 電車[でんしゃ]は北[きた]{へ}向[む]かっています。
来月[らいげつ]、大阪[おおさか]{へ}引[ひ]っ越[こ]します。
examples.en: I am moving to Osaka next month.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]が日本[にほん]{へ}遊[あそ]びに来[き]ました。
examples.en: A friend came to Japan for a visit.

contrast.note: For a destination after a motion verb, に and へ are both right. Only に marks time, where something exists, the person you meet or hand something to, a purpose (買いに行く) or a result (医者になる).
を with a motion verb marks the route you move along or the place you leave (公園を歩く, 家を出る), never the place you are heading for.
で marks where an action happens (東京で働く, I work in Tokyo); it cannot mark where you are going.

mistakes.bad: 学校[がっこう]{を}行[い]きます。
mistakes.good: 学校[がっこう]{へ}行[い]きます。
mistakes.note: 行く takes no object; the place you go to takes へ or に.

mistakes.bad: 本[ほん]を買[か]い{へ}行[い]きます。
mistakes.good: 本[ほん]を買[か]い{に}行[い]きます。
mistakes.note: A purpose (verb stem before a motion verb) takes only に, never へ.

mistakes.bad: 部屋[へや]{へ}猫[ねこ]がいます。
mistakes.good: 部屋[へや]{に}猫[ねこ]がいます。
mistakes.note: Where something is takes に; nothing is moving, so へ is impossible.

skills.tip: Can you draw an arrow to it on a map? Then へ fits. No arrow (a time, a person, a purpose, where something sits) means に.

skills.rule: To put "to / for / towards X" in front of a noun, say X への noun; にの does not exist.
skills.explain:
Japanese links a particle phrase to a following noun with の: 日本での生活, 母からの手紙. に cannot do this; にの is never correct. When the destination or recipient has to describe a noun, に switches to へ and adds の: 母への手紙 (a letter to my mother).

The noun after への is something aimed at X: things sent or said to someone (手紙, プレゼント, 質問, メッセージ), trips and routes to a place (日本への旅行, 駅への道), and feelings or effects directed at something (家族への愛, 子供への影響).

The edge is the next word. If a verb follows, drop the の: 東京へ行く or 東京に行く. If a verb describes the noun, use plain に or へ inside the clause: 東京に行く人 (people going to Tokyo), never 東京への行く人.
patterns: [person] への [手紙 / プレゼント / 質問]
[place] への [旅行 / 道 / 引っ越し]
[target] への [影響 / 愛 / 感謝]

examples.jp: 母[はは]{への}手紙[てがみ]を書[か]きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to my mother.

examples.jp: これは先生[せんせい]{への}プレゼントです。
examples.en: This is a present for the teacher.

examples.jp: 空港[くうこう]{への}道[みち]を教[おし]えてください。
examples.en: Please tell me the way to the airport.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]{への}旅行[りょこう]は楽[たの]しかったです。
examples.en: The trip to Japan was fun.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]{への}質問[しつもん]はありますか。
examples.en: Are there any questions for the company president?

examples.jp: 子供[こども]{への}影響[えいきょう]が心配[しんぱい]です。
examples.en: I am worried about the effect on the children.

contrast.note: からの is the opposite direction: 母からの手紙 is a letter from my mother, 母への手紙 a letter to her.
での marks where the noun takes place: 日本での生活 is life in Japan, 日本への旅行 a trip to Japan.
との is "with", for something shared by both sides: 友達との約束 is a promise made with a friend, 友達へのプレゼント a present for a friend.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]{にの}手紙[てがみ]を読[よ]みました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]{への}手紙[てがみ]を読[よ]みました。
mistakes.note: に can never be followed by の; before a noun, use への.

mistakes.bad: 東京[とうきょう]{への}行[い]きます。
mistakes.good: 東京[とうきょう]{へ}行[い]きます。
mistakes.note: への only stands before a noun; before a verb, drop the の.

mistakes.bad: 大学[だいがく]{への}生活[せいかつ]は楽[たの]しいです。
mistakes.good: 大学[だいがく]{での}生活[せいかつ]は楽[たの]しいです。
mistakes.note: University life happens at the university; it is not aimed at it, so use での.

skills.tip: Is the next word a noun? Then the arrow needs への. Is it a verb? Then just へ or に.
